# C++ audit 01: Prefix sums with an out-of-bounds write

**Date:** 2026-11-26
**Bug class:** out-of-bounds access (heap buffer overflow)
**Sanitizer that reproduces it:** AddressSanitizer (`-fsanitize=address`)
**Generated by:** an AI coding assistant, from the prompt below, for this repository
**Files:** [`buggy.cpp`](buggy.cpp) (generated code + test driver), [`fixed.cpp`](fixed.cpp)

## Task given to the model

```text
Write a C++ function that answers many range-sum queries on a vector<int> quickly. Each query is a pair [l, r] inclusive.
```

## Generated code (the part that matters)

```cpp
std::vector<long long> prefix(values.size());  // prefix[i] = sum of first i values
for (std::size_t i = 0; i < values.size(); ++i) {
    prefix[i + 1] = prefix[i] + values[i];
}
...
answers.push_back(prefix[r + 1] - prefix[l]);
```

## Without a sanitizer: the bug is invisible

Built with plain `clang++ -O0` and `-O2`, the program printed `all range sums correct` and exited 0 on every run. The bad write lands in heap memory just past the vector, which happened to be unused padding. A test suite that only checks answers would pass this code.

## Reproduction

```sh
clang++ -std=c++17 -g -fsanitize=address buggy.cpp -o buggy && ./buggy
```

```text
==88==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow on address 0x506000000060 ...
WRITE of size 8 at 0x506000000060 thread T0
    #0 ... in range_sums(...) 01-prefix-sum-out-of-bounds/buggy.cpp:13
    #1 ... in main 01-prefix-sum-out-of-bounds/buggy.cpp:25
0x506000000060 is located 0 bytes after 64-byte region [0x506000000020,0x506000000060)
allocated by thread T0 here:
    ...
    #6 ... in std::vector<long long>::vector(unsigned long, ...) stl_vector.h:557
```

How to read it: a **write** of 8 bytes (one `long long`) happened **0 bytes after** a 64-byte block. 64 bytes is 8 `long long`s, which is the 8-element `prefix` vector. So line 13 wrote `prefix[8]` into a vector whose last valid index is 7.

## Root cause

The comment defines `prefix[i]` as "the sum of the first `i` values", for `i = 0 … n`. That's **n + 1** values, but the vector is sized `n`. On the last loop iteration, `prefix[i + 1]` is `prefix[n]`, one past the end. `operator[]` does no bounds check, so the result is undefined behavior, not an exception.

The query line has the same off-by-one: `prefix[r + 1]` with `r = n - 1` reads `prefix[n]`. The write on line 13 just happens first.

| # | Severity | Location | Issue | How I confirmed it |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | critical | line 11 | `prefix` sized `n` instead of `n + 1`, so line 13 writes one past the end | ASan report above |
| 2 | critical | line 18 | `prefix[r + 1]` reads one past the end for `r = n - 1` (same root cause) | follows from 1; fixed by the same change |
| 3 | major | line 17 | No validation that `0 <= l <= r < n`; a bad query is silent UB | code reading |
| 4 | minor | — | Test answers were correct, so the generated "it works" claim was untested against memory errors | plain build passed |

## Fix

Size the vector `n + 1` and value-initialise it:

```cpp
std::vector<long long> prefix(values.size() + 1, 0);
```

`fixed.cpp` runs clean under ASan and its self-check passes. For untrusted queries I would also check the bounds (`at()` or an explicit range check).

## Verdict

**Reject.** The algorithm is right but every call corrupts the heap, and normal tests can't see it.

## What I would tell the model next time

"State the size of every array you index with `i + 1`, and include a test compiled with `-fsanitize=address`."
